findings.issue: Same-key permission is required, but full attack fallback plus costless utility at identical damage/geometry can strictly dominate the other key. A paid non-damage Space replacing JK also loses one damage opportunity, so some roles may rationally avoid Space.
revision: Do not fix dominance with forced alternation, alternation multipliers or combo resources. Give J and K explicit situational geometry or damage-versus-utility tradeoffs. A valid repeating key remains usable.
When a weak K function succeeds, debit its benefit from the same action budget; do not automatically retain the other key full damage plus utility. Budget-empty K still attacks.
Mark shared one-success-per-beat and Space-replaces-JK as a playtest hypothesis, not a user requirement. State lost JK opportunity in Space value evaluation.

If that candidate is adopted, failed Space cannot consume the successful slot, but a JK fallback requires its own valid input within that same window; no automatic attack from a failed Space and no carry into a later beat. Simultaneous-key arbitration remains unresolved.

needs_playtest: whether either key or always-JK strategy dominates in encounters
whether support/healer Space feels worth its MP and lost slot

findings.issue: D_n≈R_target*adjacent_interval only normalizes direct base output if interval means the designed local grid interval. Time since last successful hit would bank missed notes into large attacks; rests/track changes can create outlier intervals. Attack speed may also be counted twice through old _basic cooldown/rally logic.
revision: Use the nominal interval associated with the selected admissible beat slot, including intervening missed beats. Never use elapsed time since last accepted action or last confirmed hit. No missed-slot damage banking.

Define first-slot, tempo-change, silence and cue-change boundaries. Do not let a long rest or discontinuous music seek become one huge damage multiplier; exceptional boundary handling is a research requirement, not a settled implementation.
Use attack*speed exactly once in R_target, including agreed buffs. Existing _basic 1/speed cooldown and rally cooldown division must not separately lock or multiply the JK lane.
Apply per-action geometry/power coefficients explicitly and compare expected single-target/area budgets. Formula does not preserve total party balance or fixed losses from misses/target travel.
findings.research_delivery: dimensionally consistent candidate plus assumptions/boundary cases
needs_playtest: fast versus slow tracks with same actor and input accuracy
slow heavy roles versus fast light roles
tempo boundaries and missed-beat damage perception

findings.issue: A weak utility can be bounded per action yet unbounded per second, target or repeated swap. Reusing current HEAL scaling or max-duration slow refresh every beat creates much stronger effects than intended.
revision: Keep the proposed actual-time and total-allowance limits source-scoped across repeated notes, recipients and swaps; pause does not recharge and switching does not reset. Utility exhaustion suppresses only bonus, never K response.

For F03, sum free front-K and current periodic support when evaluating sustain; no free overheal shield, revival or MP creation. Do not reuse full HEAL power+1.5*level per note. Healing success trades away attack budget.
For F11, budget slow strength-times-duration and per-target coverage; current max(strength)/max(duration) refresh is not enough to prevent permanent control.
For F05, transfer debits source pool before crediting neighbor, conserves total remaining damage, retains remaining life and never counts as a new paid/direct hit. Empty pool still permits base K.
Do not infer that finite rate alone prevents indefinite stalling recovery; total encounter recovery and repeated encounter/retreat boundaries remain explicit risks.
findings.research_delivery: conservation bounds and failure examples; weak K candidates remain alternatives
needs_playtest: whether healing trades damage meaningfully or makes no-MP stalling dominant
curse relocation readability and practical value

findings.issue: Keeping once-per-cast counting and old support seconds CD prevents duplicate events but does not make trigger output tempo-invariant. More accepted low-damage casts can fill mark thresholds sooner; fixed per-cast temper sparks can scale with tempo even if direct D_n is normalized.
revision: Retain once-per-cast and confirmed-hit semantics, source attribution and secondary recursion guards. A multi-target or visual multi-hit action may not count as multiple baseline casts.
Explicitly audit mark, ammo follow-up, curse refresh and temper spark separately against slow/fast accepted-hit rates. Old seconds CD bounds bursts but is not proof of equal output.
For any new JK-scaled secondary damage component, either include it in the same per-slot output budget or keep its real-time limiter; do not add a new combo reward or free full support per note.
Free JK never updates last_payer or enters on_paid. Utility effects or transferred pools may not fabricate confirmed direct hits to refill these chains.
findings.research_delivery: dependency/risk matrix and explicit exclusion from direct-DPS claim
needs_playtest: actual mark/support rates across tracks and accuracy
feedback legibility under faster event density

findings.issue: Combining two techniques into one Space changes timing/range/function choice, not merely key count. It can also accidentally invoke payment-linked traits twice if implemented as two old casts.
revision: One Space means one accepted action, one actual MP transaction and one on_paid call. Subpayloads keep attribution and explicit secondary/no-recursion policy; do not implement as two independent old _cast calls.
Budget total damage, area, control, recovery and persistent effects together; old maximum cost or old maximum cooldown alone does not justify both complete effects.

For each actor retain the existing legacy_function_loss_or_pending field. F03 loses independent immediate ward timing; F11 loses independent near-frost/far-star choice; F04 loses separate settle/supply timing unless the consolidated action explicitly handles empty accounts.

Treat pre-battle original-skill choice only as a comparison alternative. If consolidated Space erases an essential role decision, report that conflict rather than silently granting both full effects or adding a menu as assumed default.
Space on-beat failure, insufficient MP or transaction failure has zero debit/effects/paid-chain activity. Low level or missing special resources may weaken optional components but cannot lock J/K.
